title: Lehmer-number minimality conjecture
statement: If L(x)=x^10+x^9−x^7−x^6−x^5−x^4−x^3+x+1, then every noncyclotomic integer polynomial P with M(P)>1 has M(P)≥M(L).

counterexample.description: A noncyclotomic integer polynomial \(P\) with \(1<M(P)<1.176280818\ldots\), refuting the stronger claim that Lehmer’s degree-10 example is minimal. Cyclotomic tests and rigorous root isolation yield a finite exact certificate.
